actionability.justification: The remedy specifies a concrete behavior change — run the declared verification command, report the actual observed result, and explicitly state when something has not been run instead of asserting success.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: Widening the scope from 'release' to 'fix, check, test, lint run, or release' covers the full incident cluster (unverified fixes, skipped tests/lint/checks) while remaining a concrete, enforceable rule rather than a vague platitude.

leakage.justification: The remedy text is fully generic (no tool names, project nouns, or incident-specific phrasing like 'fake suite' bleed into the operative instruction) and the retained 'Fake Release Discipline' header is pre-existing R2 framing rather than newly injected evidence detail.

routing_fitness.justification: Correctly avoids creating a new skill or duplicating into R1/R5/R8 by consolidating into the cheapest already-installed remedy (R2), which is the right fit for a global behavioral rule of this kind.

trigger_quality.justification: Not a skill so no formal 'Use when...' header is expected, but the text itself opens with a clear applicability condition ('Before reporting any fix, check, test, lint run, or release as complete'), which functions as an adequate inline trigger.
